title: 2 Kings Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 9.

questions.question: Who did Elisha the prophet send to anoint Jehu king over Israel?
options: One of the children of the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: One of the children of the prophets
questions.explanation: Elisha called one of the children of the prophets to carry the box of oil and anoint Jehu (2 Kings 9:1).

questions.question: Where was Jehu anointed king over Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Ramothgilead
questions.explanation: The young prophet was sent to Ramothgilead to anoint Jehu king over Israel (2 Kings 9:1, 4).

questions.question: What was the prophet instructed to do immediately after anointing Jehu?
options: Open the door and flee, and tarry not
questions.correctAnswer: Open the door and flee, and tarry not
questions.explanation: The prophet was told to open the door, flee, and not delay after anointing Jehu (2 Kings 9:3).

questions.question: What relation was Jehu to Jehoshaphat and Nimshi?
options: Jehu was the son of Jehoshaphat, who was the son of Nimshi
Jehu was the brother of Jehoshaphat
Jehu was the servant of Nimshi
Jehu was the cousin of Jehoshaphat
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu was the son of Jehoshaphat, who was the son of Nimshi
questions.explanation: Jehu is described as the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi (2 Kings 9:2).

questions.question: What did the prophet pour on Jehu's head?
questions.correctAnswer: Oil
questions.explanation: The prophet poured the box of oil on Jehu's head to anoint him king (2 Kings 9:3, 6).

questions.question: What was Jehu commanded to smite?
questions.correctAnswer: The house of Ahab
questions.explanation: Jehu was commanded to smite the house of Ahab to avenge the prophets' blood (2 Kings 9:7).

questions.question: According to the LORD, what would happen to Jezebel?
options: The dogs shall eat her in the portion of Jezreel
She would be buried by her servants
questions.correctAnswer: The dogs shall eat her in the portion of Jezreel
questions.explanation: The LORD said that dogs would eat Jezebel in Jezreel and none would bury her (2 Kings 9:10).

questions.question: What did the servants do after hearing Jehu was anointed king?
options: They took their garments and blew trumpets declaring Jehu king
They sent a message to Joram
questions.correctAnswer: They took their garments and blew trumpets declaring Jehu king
questions.explanation: The servants put their garments under Jehu on the stairs and blew trumpets, saying Jehu is king (2 Kings 9:13).

questions.question: True or False: Jehu was anointed king over the people of the LORD, even over Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The prophet said, 'I have anointed thee king over the people of the LORD, even over Israel' (2 Kings 9:6).

questions.question: True or False: Jehu was instructed to spare the house of Ahab.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jehu was commanded to smite the house of Ahab and cause its destruction (2 Kings 9:7-9).

questions.question: True or False: The young prophet who anointed Jehu fled immediately after anointing him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: After pouring oil on Jehu's head, the young prophet opened the door and fled without delay (2 Kings 9:10).

questions.question: True or False: When Jehu came out after being anointed, the servants immediately accepted it without question.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The servants questioned why the 'mad fellow' came, doubting the prophecy at first (2 Kings 9:11-12).

questions.question: Who was Jehu commanded to avenge by smiting the house of Ahab?
options: The prophets and servants of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The prophets and servants of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jehu was to avenge the blood of the prophets and servants of the LORD killed by Jezebel and Ahab's house (2 Kings 9:7).

questions.question: What did the prophet tell Jehu when anointing him king?
options: Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I have anointed thee king over Israel
Build a new altar to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I have anointed thee king over Israel
questions.explanation: The prophet said exactly this when pouring oil on Jehu's head (2 Kings 9:6).

questions.question:
In what order did these events occur? 
1) The prophet anointed Jehu
2) The servants blew trumpets declaring Jehu king
3) The prophet fled immediately after anointing Jehu
4) The prophet was sent to Ramothgilead
questions.explanation: First the prophet was sent to Ramothgilead (4), then he anointed Jehu (1), fled immediately (3), and then the servants declared Jehu king with trumpets (2) (2 Kings 9:1, 3, 10, 13).

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was Jehu's primary mission as given by the LORD through Elisha's prophet?
options: To anoint himself king over Judah
To smite the house of Ahab and avenge the prophets' blood
To make peace with the king of Syria
questions.correctAnswer: To smite the house of Ahab and avenge the prophets' blood
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:6-7 explains that Jehu was anointed king over Israel and was commanded to smite the house of Ahab to avenge the blood of the prophets and servants of the LORD.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 9, what would happen to Jezebel as prophesied?
options: She would reign as queen for many years
The dogs would eat her in the portion of Jezreel and none would bury her
She would be taken captive to Syria
She would be hidden away by her servants
questions.correctAnswer: The dogs would eat her in the portion of Jezreel and none would bury her
questions.explanation: Verse 10 states the dogs shall eat Jezebel in Jezreel and no one shall bury her, fulfilling the prophecy of divine judgment.

questions.question: How did Jehu respond when asked if he brought peace to the king's men sent to meet him at Jezreel?
options: He assured them peace had come
He told them to turn behind him and questioned their concern for peace
He ignored them and rode past
questions.correctAnswer: He told them to turn behind him and questioned their concern for peace
questions.explanation: Verses 18 and 19 show Jehu responding to the horsemen with 'What hast thou to do with peace? turn thee behind me,' signaling hostility rather than peace.

questions.question: What reason did Jehu give for killing King Joram (Jehoram) of Israel?
options: Because Joram was allied with the king of Syria
Because of the whoredoms of Jezebel and her witchcrafts
Because Joram tried to kill Jehu
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the whoredoms of Jezebel and her witchcrafts
questions.explanation: In verse 22, Jehu explicitly states that there is no peace as long as Jezebel's whoredoms and witchcrafts remain, implying Joram's complicity.

questions.question: Based on 2 Kings 9:24-26, what biblical principle about justice and accountability can be drawn from Jehu's actions towards Joram?
options: Leaders should be judged according to the Lord’s commands and previous burdens
Violence is always justified if done in anger
One should always seek peace even with enemies
Justice should be delayed until full investigation
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders should be judged according to the Lord’s commands and previous burdens
questions.explanation: Verses 25-26 show Jehu reminding his captain of the Lord's burden upon Ahab’s house and the blood of Naboth, showing obedience to divine judgment and justice.

questions.question: What does Jehu’s command to prevent anyone from escaping the city to Jezreel (verse 15) teach about obedience and thoroughness in executing God’s will?
options: Partial obedience is acceptable if circumstances require
Complete obedience and preventing escape ensures God's judgment is fulfilled
Disobedience can be overlooked in difficult times
Compromise is necessary to avoid unnecessary bloodshed
questions.correctAnswer: Complete obedience and preventing escape ensures God's judgment is fulfilled
questions.explanation: Verse 15 shows Jehu’s insistence that none escape to warn Jezreel, highlighting the importance of full obedience to God's command for His will to be accomplished.

questions.question: True or False: Jehu’s furious driving of his chariot was a sign to the watchman that he was a peaceful envoy.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 20 describes Jehu’s driving as furious, indicating aggression rather than peaceful intentions, which alarmed the watchman.

questions.question: Where did Jehu meet King Joram and King Ahaziah as they went out to confront him?
options: In the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite
Near the garden house in Jezreel
questions.correctAnswer: In the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite
questions.explanation: Verse 21 states that Jehu met Joram and Ahaziah in the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite, the field associated with the blood vengeance mentioned.

questions.question: What lesson about trusting God’s justice can be inferred from Jehu’s words to his captain after killing Joram?
options: Remember God’s burden and promises as motivation for obedience
Personal revenge is the highest priority
Ignore past sins when judging others
questions.correctAnswer: Remember God’s burden and promises as motivation for obedience
questions.explanation: Verses 25-26 show Jehu reminding his captain of the LORD's command and the blood of Naboth, demonstrating faithfulness to God's justice rather than personal vengeance.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 9:27-28 teach about the consequences of fleeing from God's appointed judgment?
options: Fleeing will not prevent the fulfillment of God's judgment and leads to death
God always forgives those who escape judgment
Judgment can be avoided through diplomacy
questions.correctAnswer: Fleeing will not prevent the fulfillment of God's judgment and leads to death
questions.explanation: Ahaziah fled but was pursued and killed as recorded in verses 27-28, showing fleeing does not escape God's judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Jehu’s killing of Jezebel was violent and fulfilled the prophecy about her fate.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verses 33-37 describe Jezebel being thrown down, trodden, and her body left for dogs, fulfilling Elijah's prophecy.

questions.question: What does Jehu's reaction to Jezebel's death and the partial remains found teach about God’s sovereignty over justice?
options: Jehu ignored the prophecy and buried her fully
Jehu recognized the fulfillment of the LORD’s word through Elijah's prophecy
Jehu decided to spare her life
Jehu hid the truth from his men
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu recognized the fulfillment of the LORD’s word through Elijah's prophecy
questions.explanation: Verse 36-37 shows Jehu acknowledging the prophecy of Elijah being fulfilled, highlighting submission to God's sovereign justice.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 9:14-16 teach about the importance of timing and preparation in fulfilling God's plans?
options: God’s plans should be rushed without preparation
Jehu delayed until he saw opportunity, showing God’s timing is perfect
Human timing is irrelevant to God’s purposes
Preparation is unnecessary if one has faith
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu delayed until he saw opportunity, showing God’s timing is perfect
questions.explanation: Verses 14-16 show Jehu conspiring and riding to Jezreel where Joram lay wounded, indicating careful timing in executing God’s will.

questions.question: True or False: Jehu’s actions in 2 Kings 9 demonstrate that God sometimes uses bold and decisive action to bring about justice and righteousness.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jehu's anointing and subsequent decisive actions against Ahab's house as described in verses 6-26 demonstrate God's use of bold action to fulfill justice.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Jehu’s confrontation with Joram and Ahaziah emphasize the biblical virtue of courage in obedience to God?
options: Jehu hesitated and sought peace first
Jehu confronted kings despite danger, exemplifying courage in obedience
Jehu negotiated a truce to avoid bloodshed
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu confronted kings despite danger, exemplifying courage in obedience
questions.explanation: Verses 21-24 reveal Jehu meeting kings in battle and killing Joram, showing courage to obey God's command despite risks.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 9.

questions.question: Where did Ahaziah flee after being wounded by Jehu's men, according to 2 Kings 9?
questions.correctAnswer: The garden house
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:27 states that Ahaziah fled by the way of the garden house when Jehu's men pursued him.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 9:28, where was Ahaziah ultimately buried after his death?
questions.correctAnswer: City of David
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:28 says Ahaziah was buried in his sepulchre with his fathers in the city of David.

questions.question: In what year of Joram's reign did Ahaziah begin to reign over Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Eleventh year
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:29 specifies that Ahaziah began to reign in the eleventh year of Joram the son of Ahab.

questions.question: How did Jezebel prepare herself when she heard Jehu was coming to Jezreel?
options: Painted her face and tired her head
questions.correctAnswer: Painted her face and tired her head
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:30 states Jezebel painted her face and tired her head to look out a window upon hearing Jehu's arrival.

questions.question: What was Jezebel's sarcastic question to Jehu as he entered the gate of Jezreel?
options: Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?
questions.correctAnswer: Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:31 records Jezebel's question referencing Zimri's assassination of his master to mock Jehu.

questions.question: Who looked out the window to Jehu when he asked, 'Who is on my side?'?
questions.correctAnswer: Two or three eunuchs
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:32 mentions that two or three eunuchs looked out to Jehu when he asked who was on his side.

questions.question: What happened to Jezebel after Jehu ordered her to be thrown down?
options: Her blood was sprinkled on the wall and horses, and she was trodden under foot
questions.correctAnswer: Her blood was sprinkled on the wall and horses, and she was trodden under foot
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:33 describes Jezebel's violent death and how her blood splattered and she was trampled.

questions.question: What did Jehu command his men to do after entering Jezreel and eating and drinking?
questions.correctAnswer: Go see and bury Jezebel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:34 shows Jehu ordering his men to bury Jezebel as she was a king's daughter.

questions.question: What parts of Jezebel's body were found when the servants tried to bury her?
options: Skull, feet, and palms of her hands
questions.correctAnswer: Skull, feet, and palms of her hands
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:35 states only Jezebel's skull, feet, and palms of her hands were found.

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophet's word did Jehu say was fulfilled by Jezebel's fate?
questions.correctAnswer: Elijah the Tishbite
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:36 states that Jehu declared the fulfillment of Elijah's prophecy concerning Jezebel.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'anointed' used in 2 Kings 9:3, relating to Jehu's appointment?
options: To smear with oil as a sign of consecration
To crown with a golden crown
questions.correctAnswer: To smear with oil as a sign of consecration
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'mashach' means to anoint by smearing oil, symbolizing consecration to office or kingship as seen in 2 Kings 9:3.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Kings 9:25-26 where Jehu recalls the blood of Naboth and his sons?
questions.correctAnswer: Allusion to past injustice
questions.explanation: These verses allude to Naboth's murder ordered by Ahab and Jezebel, foreshadowing Jehu's vengeance and fulfilling divine justice.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse echoes the theme of divine judgment against Jezebel-like figures as seen in 2 Kings 9?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 2:20
questions.explanation: Revelation 2:20 warns against a woman called Jezebel who misleads God's servants, echoing the judgment theme of 2 Kings 9.

questions.question: What does Jehu’s furious chariot driving in 2 Kings 9:20 symbolize in the broader historical and cultural context of ancient Near East warfare?
options: Relentless divine judgment and military zeal
questions.correctAnswer: Relentless divine judgment and military zeal
questions.explanation: Jehu’s furious driving typified aggressive assault and zeal for God's judgment, reflecting ancient Near Eastern warrior ethos.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 9:37, Jezebel's body was buried with honor in Jezreel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:37 states Jezebel's carcass was like dung on the field and no one would say, 'This is Jezebel,' indicating a dishonorable death and no burial.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God's command to anoint Jehu as king over Israel in 2 Kings 9:3?
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty in appointing rulers
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:3 shows God directing His prophet to anoint Jehu king, illustrating God's sovereign authority to establish leaders according to His divine purpose.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 9:7, what is the purpose of Jehu's anointing as king over Israel?
options: To bring peace between Israel and Syria
To smite the house of Ahab and avenge the blood of the prophets
To rebuild the temple of the LORD
To establish a new dynasty unrelated to Ahab
questions.correctAnswer: To smite the house of Ahab and avenge the blood of the prophets
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:7 explicitly states that Jehu's anointing is to bring judgment on Ahab's house to avenge the blood of God's servants, the prophets, and the LORD's servants, revealing God's justice.

questions.question: Which doctrine is most clearly taught by God's promise in 2 Kings 9:8-9 concerning the house of Ahab?
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of divine retribution
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 declare that the entire house of Ahab will perish as a consequence of their sins, illustrating the doctrine that God executes just retribution on unrepentant sin.

questions.question: How does Jehu's furious driving, described in 2 Kings 9:20, typify Christ's zeal in the redemptive narrative?
options: It symbolizes Christ's zeal for the purity of God's kingdom
It represents Christ's peaceful approach to sinners
It signifies Christ's patience in human weakness
It portrays Christ's avoidance of conflict
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes Christ's zeal for the purity of God's kingdom
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:20 describes Jehu's furious driving as he executes judgment, which typologically foreshadows Christ's zeal in cleansing His kingdom from sin, paralleling John 2:17.

questions.question: In 2 Kings 9:24-26, Jehu orders Joram's body to be cast into Naboth's field. What theological principle does this action emphasize?
options: God's faithfulness in keeping covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice in requiting bloodguilt
questions.explanation: Verses 24-26 demonstrate God's justice as Jehu executes the judgment prophesied against Ahab's house for shedding Naboth's blood, emphasizing divine retribution for injustice.

questions.question: What does Jezebel's fate in 2 Kings 9:33-37 reveal about God's judgment on idolatry and wickedness?
options: God's judgment is thorough and humiliating
God spares the wicked for repentance
God's judgment is secret and hidden
God rewards wickedness in this life
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is thorough and humiliating
questions.explanation: The graphic description in 2 Kings 9:33-37 shows Jezebel's body being desecrated, fulfilling Elijah's prophecy and illustrating God's complete and humiliating judgment on idolatry and wickedness.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about divine justice and prophecy is taught by 2 Kings 9:10 and 2 Kings 9:36-37?
options: God's prophetic word is sure and His justice unavoidable
God's promises are conditional on human effort
God's justice is unpredictable and arbitrary
questions.correctAnswer: God's prophetic word is sure and His justice unavoidable
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 36-37 both affirm the prophecy against Jezebel, showing that God's word through His prophets is certain and that His justice will be executed without fail.

questions.question: How do 2 Kings 9:12 and 2 Kings 9:13 together illustrate the role of divine confirmation in kingship during Israel's monarchy?
options: God confirms kingship through prophetic anointing and public acclamation
Kingship was determined solely by military power
Kingship depended on popular vote without divine input
Kingship was inherited regardless of divine approval
questions.correctAnswer: God confirms kingship through prophetic anointing and public acclamation
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:12 records the prophetic declaration of Jehu's kingship, and 9:13 shows the people's public acknowledgment, demonstrating that God's appointment is confirmed through prophecy and communal recognition.

questions.question: What theological implication arises from Jehu’s question in 2 Kings 9:22 regarding the 'whoredoms of thy mother Jezebel and her witchcrafts'?
options: Sin corrupts leadership and brings divine judgment
Witchcraft is tolerated in Israel's worship
Idolatry is insignificant in God's eyes
questions.correctAnswer: Sin corrupts leadership and brings divine judgment
questions.explanation: Jehu’s rebuke in 2 Kings 9:22 highlights how Jezebel’s sinful practices corrupted Israel’s leadership, provoking God’s judgment, emphasizing the seriousness of sin in public and spiritual authority.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s commands to Jehu to destroy Ahab’s house (2 Kings 9:7-10) reflect divine cruelty. What does 2 Kings 9:7-10 actually teach about God’s character?
options: God’s justice demands judgment against persistent evil
God is indifferent to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice demands judgment against persistent evil
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:7-10 shows that God’s command to Jehu serves to avenge the blood of His prophets, revealing His just nature in judging persistent, unrepentant evil rather than cruelty.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 9:29 teach about the historical continuity of God's providential plan through Israel's monarchy?
options: God sovereignly ordains successive reigns to fulfill His purposes
God abandons His people during monarchical transitions
Kingship in Israel was chaotic and unplanned
God’s plan is hindered by human failure
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly ordains successive reigns to fulfill His purposes
questions.explanation: The verse marks the beginning of Ahaziah’s reign, showing the providential unfolding of history through successive monarchs as part of God’s sovereign plan despite human sinfulness.

questions.question: How do 2 Kings 9:16 and 2 Kings 9:27 together reveal God’s control over human events and the fulfillment of His judgment?
options: God orchestrates the deaths of kings to execute justice
Human kings rule independently of divine will
Fate governs history apart from God
questions.correctAnswer: God orchestrates the deaths of kings to execute justice
questions.explanation: Verse 16 shows Ahaziah visiting Joram before both meet death in verse 27, demonstrating that God sovereignly controls events to bring about His judgment on unfaithful kings.

questions.question: What does the reaction of the watchman in 2 Kings 9:20 reveal about Jehu’s role in God's redemptive plan?
options: Jehu acts as a divinely empowered agent executing God’s judgment
Jehu is an unrecognized false prophet
Jehu is merely a political opportunist
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu acts as a divinely empowered agent executing God’s judgment
questions.explanation: The watchman’s observation in 2 Kings 9:20 emphasizes Jehu’s distinctive furious driving as a sign he is carrying out God’s appointed judgment, marking him as an instrument of divine justice.

questions.question: What combined theological truth about divine judgment and prophetic fulfillment is taught by 2 Kings 9:33 and 2 Kings 9:37?
options: God's judgment fulfills prophecy and manifests His holiness
Prophecy is symbolic without literal fulfillment
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment fulfills prophecy and manifests His holiness
questions.explanation: These verses narrate the literal fulfillment of Elijah's prophecy against Jezebel, showing God's faithfulness to His word and His commitment to holiness by punishing sin visibly.

questions.question: What narrative role does Jehu's anointing and subsequent actions in 2 Kings 9 reveal in the context of Israel's history of covenant unfaithfulness?
options: Jehu is God's instrument to purge idolatry and renew covenant faithfulness
Jehu establishes a new idolatrous dynasty
Jehu's reign marks the end of Israel's monarchy
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu is God's instrument to purge idolatry and renew covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: The chapter shows Jehu anointed to destroy Ahab’s house and Jezebel’s idolatry, acting as God's agent to bring covenant renewal by removing unfaithfulness from Israel’s leadership.
